requirements.name: Auto Scaling launch config public IP should be disabled
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS EC2 Auto Scaling groups have public IP addresses enabled through Launch Configurations. This rule is non-compliant if the Launch Configuration for an Auto Scaling group has AssociatePublicIpAddress set to 'true'.

requirements.name: Log group retention period should be at least 365 days
requirements.description: Ensure a minimum duration of event log data is retained for your log groups to help with troubleshooting and forensics investigations.

requirements.name: DMS replication instances should not be publicly accessible
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring DMS replication instances cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: EBS snapshots should not be publicly restorable
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring EBS snapshots are not publicly restorable.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should have IAM profile attached
requirements.description: Ensure that an AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instance has an Identity and Access Management (IAM) profile attached to it. This rule is non-compliant if no IAM profile is attached to the AWS EC2 instance.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should be in a VPC
requirements.description: Deploy AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances within an AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC) to enable secure communication between an instance and other services within the amazon VPC, without requiring an internet gateway, NAT device, or VPN connection.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should not have a public IP address
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should use IMDSv2
requirements.description: Ensure the Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) method is enabled to help protect access and control of AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instance metadata.

requirements.name: ECS task definition container definitions should be checked for host mode
requirements.description: Check if AWS Elastic Container Service (AWS ECS) task definition with host networking mode has 'privileged' or 'user' container definitions.The rule is non-compliant for task definitions with host network mode and container definitions of privileged=false or empty and user=root or empty.

requirements.name: EKS clusters endpoint should restrict public access
requirements.description: Ensure whether AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service (AWS EKS) endpoint is not publicly accessible. The rule is compliant if the endpoint is publicly accessible.

requirements.name: EMR cluster Kerberos should be enabled
requirements.description: The access permissions and authorizations can be managed and incorporated with the principles of least privilege and separation of duties, by enabling Kerberos for AWS EMR clusters.

requirements.name: EMR cluster master nodes should not have public IP addresses
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS EMR cluster master nodes cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: ES domains should be in a VPC
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS Elasticsearch Service (AWS ES) Domains are within an AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC).

requirements.name: Ensure IAM policy should not grant full access to service
requirements.description: Checks if AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies grant permissions to all actions on individual AWS resources. The rule is non-compliant if the managed IAM policy allows full access to at least 1 AWS service.

requirements.name: IAM groups should have at least one user
requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties with access permissions and authorizations, by ensuring that IAM groups have at least one IAM user.

requirements.name: IAM groups, users, and roles should not have any inline policies
requirements.description: Ensure an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) user, IAM role or IAM group does not have an inline policy to control access to systems and assets.

requirements.name: IAM customer managed policies should be attached to IAM role
requirements.description: This control checks if customer managed IAM policies are attached to an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role. The rule is non-compliant if a customer managed IAM policy is not attached to any IAM role.

requirements.name: IAM policy should not have statements with admin access
requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties with access permissions and authorizations, restricting policies from containing 'Effect': 'Allow' with 'Action': '*' over 'Resource': '*'.

requirements.name: IAM customer managed policy should be in use
requirements.description: This control checks whether customer managed IAM policies are attached to an IAM user, or a group with one or more IAM users, or an IAM role with one or more trusted entity.

requirements.name: IAM root user should not have access keys
requirements.description: Access to systems and assets can be controlled by checking that the root user does not have access keys attached to their AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role.

requirements.name: IAM users should be in at least one group
requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you restrict access permissions and authorizations, by ensuring IAM users are members of at least one group.

requirements.name: IAM user should not have any inline or attached policies
requirements.description: This rule ensures AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies are attached only to groups or roles to control access to systems and assets.

requirements.name: Lambda functions should be in a VPC
requirements.description: Deploy AWS Lambda functions within an AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC) for a secure communication between a function and other services within the AWS VPC.

requirements.name: Lambda functions should restrict public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS Lambda functions cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: RDS DB instances should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are not public.

requirements.name: RDS snapshots should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are not public.

requirements.name: Redshift clusters should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Redshift clusters are not public.

requirements.name: S3 bucket policy should prohibit public access
requirements.description: This control checks that the access granted by the S3 bucket is restricted by any of the principals, federated users, service principals, IP addresses, or VPCs that you provide. The rule is compliant if a bucket policy is not present.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should prohibit public read access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by only allowing authorized users, processes, and devices access to AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should prohibit public write access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by only allowing authorized users, processes, and devices access to AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 public access should be blocked at account level
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: S3 public access should be blocked at bucket levels
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets are publicly accessible. This rule is non-compliant if an AWS S3 bucket is not listed in the excludedPublicBuckets parameter and bucket level settings are public.

requirements.name: SageMaker notebook instances should not have direct internet access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS SageMaker notebooks do not allow direct internet access.

requirements.name: SSM documents should not be public
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS Systems Manager documents that are owned by the account are public. This control fails if SSM documents with the owner Self are public.

requirements.name: VPC subnet auto assign public IP should be disabled
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC) subnets are assigned a public IP address. The control is compliant if AWS VPC does not have subnets that are assigned a public IP address. The control is non-compliant if AWS VPC has subnets that are assigned a public IP address.

requirements.name: AWS account should be part of AWS Organizations
requirements.description: Ensure that an AWS account is part of AWS Organizations. The rule is non-compliant if an AWS account is not part of AWS Organizations or AWS Organizations master account ID does not match rule parameter MasterAccountId.

requirements.name: At least one trail should be enabled with security best practices
requirements.description: This rule helps ensure the use of AWS recommended security best practices for AWS CloudTrail, by checking for the enablement of multiple settings. These include the use of log encryption, log validation, and enabling AWS CloudTrail in multiple regions.

requirements.name: EBS volumes should be attached to EC2 instances
requirements.description: Checks if EBS volumes are attached to EC2 instances.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift should have required maintenance settings
requirements.description: Ensure whether AWS Redshift clusters have the specified maintenance settings. Redshift clusters `allowVersionUpgrade` should be set to `true` and `automatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod` should be greater than 7.

requirements.name: Auto Scaling groups with a load balancer should use health checks
requirements.description: The Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) health checks for AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Auto Scaling groups support maintenance of adequate capacity and availability.

requirements.name: At least one multi-region AWS CloudTrail should be present in an account
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail records AWS Management Console actions and API calls. You can identify which users and accounts called AWS, the source IP address from where the calls were made, and when the calls occurred. CloudTrail will deliver log files from all AWS Regions to your S3 bucket if MULTI_REGION_CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED is enabled.

requirements.name: All S3 buckets should log S3 data events in CloudTrail
requirements.description: The collection of Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) data events helps in detecting any anomalous activity. The details include AWS account information that accessed an AWS S3 bucket, IP address, and time of event.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trails should be integrated with CloudWatch logs
requirements.description: Use AWS CloudWatch to centrally collect and manage log event activity. Inclusion of AWS CloudTrail data provides details of API call activity within your AWS account.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trail logs should be encrypted with KMS CMK
requirements.description: To help protect sensitive data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS CloudWatch Log Groups.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trail log file validation should be enabled
requirements.description: Utilize AWS CloudTrail log file validation to check the integrity of CloudTrail logs. Log file validation helps determine if a log file was modified or deleted or unchanged after CloudTrail delivered it. This feature is built using industry standard algorithms: SHA-256 for hashing and SHA-256 with RSA for digital signing. This makes it computationally infeasible to modify, delete or forge CloudTrail log files without detection.

requirements.name: Attached EBS volumes should have encryption enabled
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes.

requirements.name: EBS encryption by default should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes.

requirements.name: IAM password policies for users should have strong configurations
requirements.description: The identities and the credentials are issued, managed, and verified based on an organizational IAM password policy.

requirements.name: IAM root user hardware MFA should be enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring hardware MFA is enabled for the root user.

requirements.name: IAM root user MFA should be enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring MFA is enabled for the root user.

requirements.name: IAM users with console access should have MFA enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that MFA is enabled for all AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users that have a console password.

requirements.name: KMS CMK rotation should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable key rotation to ensure that keys are rotated once they have reached the end of their crypto period.

requirements.name: S3 bucket cross-region replication should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) Cross-Region Replication (CRR) supports maintaining adequate capacity and availability.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should enforce SSL
requirements.description: To help protect data in transit, ensure that your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets require requests to use Secure Socket Layer (SSL).

requirements.name: S3 bucket logging should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) server access logging provides a method to monitor the network for potential cybersecurity events.

requirements.name: VPC default security group should not allow inbound and outbound traffic
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) security groups can help in the management of network access by providing stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources.

requirements.name: VPC flow logs should be enabled
requirements.description: The VPC flow logs provide detailed records for information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress SSH access from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Security Groups can help manage network access by providing stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources.

requirements.name: IAM user MFA should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable this rule to restrict access to resources in the AWS Cloud.

requirements.name: IAM user credentials that have not been used in 90 days should be disabled
requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you with access permissions and authorizations by checking for IAM passwords and access keys that are not used for a specified time period.

requirements.name: AWS Security Hub should be enabled for an AWS Account
requirements.description: AWS Security Hub helps to monitor unauthorized personnel, connections, devices, and software. AWS Security Hub aggregates, organizes, and prioritizes the security alerts, or findings, from multiple AWS services.

requirements.name: SSM managed instance patching should be compliant
requirements.description: Enable this rule to help with identification and documentation of AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) vulnerabilities.

requirements.name: API Gateway stage logging should be enabled
requirements.description: API Gateway logging displays detailed views of users who accessed the API and the way they accessed the API.

requirements.name: CloudFront distributions access logs should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if AWS CloudFront distributions are configured to capture information from AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) server access logs. This rule is non-compliant if a CloudFront distribution does not have logging configured.

requirements.name: At least one enabled trail should be present in a region
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail can help in non-repudiation by recording AWS Management Console actions and API calls. You can identify the users and AWS accounts that called an AWS service, the source IP address where the calls generated, and the timings of the calls. Details of captured data are seen within AWS CloudTrail Record Contents.

requirements.name: ELB application and classic load balancer logging should be enabled
requirements.description: Elastic Load Balancing activity is a central point of communication within an environment.

requirements.name: Elasticsearch domain should send logs to CloudWatch
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS OpenSearch Service (OpenSearch Service) domains are configured to send logs to AWS CloudWatch Logs. The rule is compliant if a log is enabled for an OpenSearch Service domain. This rule is non-compliant if logging is not configured.

requirements.name: Database logging should be enabled
requirements.description: To help with logging and monitoring within your environment, ensure AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) logging is enabled.

requirements.name: Redshift cluster audit logging and encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Redshift clusters. You must also ensure that required configurations are deployed on AWS Redshift clusters. The audit logging should be enabled to provide information about connections and user activities in the database.

requirements.name: WAF web ACL logging should be enabled
requirements.description: To help with logging and monitoring within your environment, enable AWS WAF logging on regional and global web ACLs.

requirements.name: Logging should be enabled on AWS WAFv2 regional and global web access control list (ACLs)
requirements.description: To help with logging and monitoring within your environment, enable AWS WAF (V2) logging on regional and global web ACLs.

requirements.name: DynamoDB tables should be in a backup plan
requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS DynamoDB tables are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: DynamoDB table point-in-time recovery should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable this rule to check that information has been backed up. It also maintains the backups by ensuring that point-in-time recovery is enabled in AWS DynamoDB.

requirements.name: EBS volumes should be in a backup plan
requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: EC2 instance should have EBS optimization enabled
requirements.description: An optimized instance in AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) provides additional, dedicated capacity for AWS EBS I/O operations.

requirements.name: EFS file systems should be in a backup plan
requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Elastic File System (AWS EFS) file systems are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: ElastiCache Redis cluster automatic backup should be enabled with retention period of 15 days or greater
requirements.description: When automatic backups are enabled, AWS ElastiCache creates a backup of the cluster on a daily basis. The backup can be retained for a number of days as specified by your organization. Automatic backups can help guard against data loss.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance backup should be enabled
requirements.description: The backup feature of AWS RDS creates backups of your databases and transaction logs.

requirements.name: RDS DB instances should be in a backup plan
requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift clusters should have automatic snapshots enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS Redshift clusters have automated snapshots enabled. It also checks whether the snapshot retention period is greater than or equal to seven.

requirements.name: S3 bucket versioning should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) bucket versioning helps keep multiple variants of an object in the same AWS S3 bucket.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should be managed by AWS Systems Manager
requirements.description: An inventory of the software platforms and applications within the organization is possible by managing AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances with AWS Systems Manager.

requirements.description: The "root" account has unrestricted access to all resources in the AWS account. It is highly recommended that the use of this account be avoided.

requirements.name: 1.2 Ensure multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for all IAM users that have a console password
requirements.description: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an extra layer of protection on top of a user name and password. With MFA enabled, when a user signs in to an AWS website, they will be prompted for their user name and password as well as for an authentication code from their AWS MFA device. It is recommended that MFA be enabled for all accounts that have a console password.

requirements.name: 1.3 Ensure credentials unused for 90 days or greater are disabled
requirements.description: AWS IAM users can access AWS resources using different types of credentials, such as passwords or access keys. It is recommended that all credentials that have been unused in 90 or greater days be removed or deactivated.

requirements.name: 1.4 Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less
requirements.description: Access keys consist of an access key ID and secret access key, which are used to sign programmatic requests that you make to AWS. AWS users need their own access keys to make programmatic calls to AWS from the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), Tools for Windows PowerShell, the AWS SDKs, or direct HTTP calls using the APIs for individual AWS services. It is recommended that all access keys be regularly rotated.

requirements.name: 1.5 Ensure IAM password policy requires at least one uppercase letter
requirements.description: Password policies are, in part, used to enforce password complexity requirements. IAM password policies can be used to ensure password are comprised of different character sets. It is recommended that the password policy require at least one uppercase letter.

requirements.name: 1.6 Ensure IAM password policy require at least one lowercase letter
requirements.description: Password policies are, in part, used to enforce password complexity requirements. IAM password policies can be used to ensure password are comprised of different character sets. It is recommended that the password policy require at least one lowercase letter.

requirements.name: 1.7 Ensure IAM password policy require at least one symbol
requirements.description: Password policies are, in part, used to enforce password complexity requirements. IAM password policies can be used to ensure password are comprised of different character sets. It is recommended that the password policy require at least one symbol.

requirements.name: 1.8 Ensure IAM password policy require at least one number
requirements.description: Password policies are, in part, used to enforce password complexity requirements. IAM password policies can be used to ensure password are comprised of different character sets. It is recommended that the password policy require at least one number.

requirements.name: 1.9 Ensure IAM password policy requires minimum length of 14 or greater
requirements.description: Password policies are, in part, used to enforce password complexity requirements. IAM password policies can be used to ensure password are at least a given length. It is recommended that the password policy require a minimum password length 14.

requirements.name: 1.10 Ensure IAM password policy prevents password reuse
requirements.description: IAM password policies can prevent the reuse of a given password by the same user. It is recommended that the password policy prevent the reuse of passwords.

requirements.name: 1.11 Ensure IAM password policy expires passwords within 90 days or less
requirements.description: IAM password policies can require passwords to be rotated or expired after a given number of days. It is recommended that the password policy expire passwords after 90 days or less.

requirements.name: 1.12 Ensure no root account access key exists
requirements.description: The root account is the most privileged user in an AWS account. AWS Access Keys provide programmatic access to a given AWS account. It is recommended that all access keys associated with the root account be removed.

requirements.name: 1.13 Ensure MFA is enabled for the "root" account
requirements.description: The root account is the most privileged user in an AWS account. MFA adds an extra layer of protection on top of a user name and password. With MFA enabled, when a user signs in to an AWS website, they will be prompted for their user name and password as well as for an authentication code from their AWS MFA device.

requirements.name: 1.14 Ensure hardware MFA is enabled for the "root" account
requirements.description: The root account is the most privileged user in an AWS account. MFA adds an extra layer of protection on top of a user name and password. With MFA enabled, when a user signs in to an AWS website, they will be prompted for their user name and password as well as for an authentication code from their AWS MFA device. For Level 2, it is recommended that the root account be protected with a hardware MFA.

requirements.name: 1.15 Ensure security questions are registered in the AWS account
requirements.description: The AWS support portal allows account owners to establish security questions that can be used to authenticate individuals calling AWS customer service for support. It is recommended that security questions be established.

requirements.name: 1.16 Ensure IAM policies are attached only to groups or roles
requirements.description: By default, IAM users, groups, and roles have no access to AWS resources. IAM policies are the means by which privileges are granted to users, groups, or roles. It is recommended that IAM policies be applied directly to groups and roles but not users.

requirements.name: 1.17 Maintain current contact details
requirements.description: Ensure contact email and telephone details for AWS accounts are current and map to more than one individual in your organization. An AWS account supports a number of contact details, and AWS will use these to contact the account owner if activity judged to be in breach of Acceptable Use Policy or indicative of likely security compromise is observed by the AWS Abuse team. Contact details should not be for a single individual, as circumstances may arise where that individual is unavailable.

requirements.name: 1.18 Ensure security contact information is registered
requirements.description: AWS provides customers with the option of specifying the contact information for account's security team. It is recommended that this information be provided.

requirements.name: 1.19 Ensure IAM instance roles are used for AWS resource access from instances
requirements.description: AWS access from within AWS instances can be done by either encoding AWS keys into AWS API calls or by assigning the instance to a role which has an appropriate permissions policy for the required access. "AWS Access" means accessing the APIs of AWS in order to access AWS resources or manage AWS account resources.

requirements.name: 1.20 Ensure a support role has been created to manage incidents with AWS Support
requirements.description: AWS provides a support center that can be used for incident notification and response, as well as technical support and customer services. Create an IAM Role to allow authorized users to manage incidents with AWS Support.

requirements.name: 1.21 Do not setup access keys during initial user setup for all IAM users that have a console password
requirements.description: AWS console defaults the checkbox for creating access keys to enabled. This results in many access keys being generated unnecessarily. In addition to unnecessary credentials, it also generates unnecessary management work in auditing and rotating these keys.

requirements.name: 1.22 Ensure IAM policies that allow full "*:*" administrative privileges are not created
requirements.description: IAM policies are the means by which privileges are granted to users, groups, or roles. It is recommended and considered a standard security advice to grant least privilege—that is, granting only the permissions required to perform a task. Determine what users need to do and then craft policies for them that let the users perform only those tasks, instead of allowing full administrative privileges.

requirements.name: 2.1 Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for your account and delivers log files to you. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service. CloudTrail provides a history of AWS API calls for an account, including API calls made via the Management Console, SDKs, command line tools, and higher-level AWS services (such as CloudFormation).

requirements.name: 2.2 Ensure CloudTrail log file validation is enabled.
requirements.description: CloudTrail log file validation creates a digitally signed digest file containing a hash of each log that CloudTrail writes to S3. These digest files can be used to determine whether a log file was changed, deleted, or unchanged after CloudTrail delivered the log. It is recommended that file validation be enabled on all CloudTrails.

requirements.name: 2.3 Ensure the S3 bucket used to store CloudTrail logs is not publicly accessible
requirements.description: CloudTrail logs a record of every API call made in your AWS account. These logs file are stored in an S3 bucket. It is recommended that the bucket policy, or access control list (ACL), applied to the S3 bucket that CloudTrail logs to prevents public access to the CloudTrail logs.

requirements.name: 2.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls made in a given AWS account. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service. CloudTrail uses Amazon S3 for log file storage and delivery, so log files are stored durably. In addition to capturing CloudTrail logs within a specified S3 bucket for long term analysis, realtime analysis can be performed by configuring CloudTrail to send logs to CloudWatch Logs. For a trail that is enabled in all regions in an account, CloudTrail sends log files from all those regions to a CloudWatch Logs log group. It is recommended that CloudTrail logs be sent to CloudWatch Logs.

requirements.name: 2.5 Ensure AWS Config is enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS Config is a web service that performs configuration management of supported AWS resources within your account and delivers log files to you. The recorded information includes the configuration item (AWS resource), relationships between configuration items (AWS resources), any configuration changes between resources. It is recommended to enable AWS Config be enabled in all regions.

requirements.name: 2.6 Ensure S3 bucket access logging is enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket
requirements.description: S3 Bucket Access Logging generates a log that contains access records for each request made to your S3 bucket. An access log record contains details about the request, such as the request type, the resources specified in the request worked, and the time and date the request was processed. It is recommended that bucket access logging be enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket.

requirements.name: 2.7 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for an account and makes those logs available to users and resources in accordance with IAM policies. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) is a managed service that helps create and control the encryption keys used to encrypt account data, and uses Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) to protect the security of encryption keys. CloudTrail logs can be configured to leverage server side encryption (SSE) and KMS customer created master keys (CMK) to further protect CloudTrail logs. It is recommended that CloudTrail be configured to use SSE-KMS.

requirements.name: 2.8 Ensure rotation for customer created CMKs is enabled
requirements.description: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) allows customers to rotate the backing key which is key material stored within the KMS which is tied to the key ID of the Customer Created customer master key (CMK). It is the backing key that is used to perform cryptographic operations such as encryption and decryption. Automated key rotation currently retains all prior backing keys so that decryption of encrypted data can take place transparently. It is recommended that CMK key rotation be enabled.

requirements.name: 2.9 Ensure VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs

requirements.name: 1.9 Ensure IAM password policy prevents password reuse

requirements.name: 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 90 days or greater are disabled

requirements.name: 1.13 Ensure there is only one active access key available for any single IAM user

requirements.name: 1.14 Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less
requirements.description: Access keys consist of an access key ID and secret access key, which are used to sign programmatic requests that you make to AWS. AWS users need their own access keys to make programmatic calls to AWS from the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), Tools for Windows PowerShell, the AWS SDKs, or direct HTTP calls using the APIs for individual AWS services. It is recommended that all access keys be regularly rotated.

requirements.name: 1.15 Ensure IAM Users Receive Permissions Only Through Groups

requirements.name: 1.16 Ensure IAM policies that allow full "*:*" administrative privileges are not attached

requirements.name: 1.18 Ensure IAM instance roles are used for AWS resource access from instances

requirements.name: 1.19 Ensure that all the expired SSL/TLS certificates stored in AWS IAM are removed

IAM securely encrypts your private keys and stores the encrypted version in IAM SSL certificate storage. IAM supports deploying server certificates in all regions, but you must obtain your certificate from an external provider for use with AWS. You cannot upload an ACM certificate to IAM. Additionally, you cannot manage your certificates from the IAM Console.

requirements.name: 1.20 Ensure that S3 Buckets are configured with 'Block public access (bucket settings)'
requirements.description: Amazon S3 provides Block public access (bucket settings) and Block public access (account settings) to help you manage public access to Amazon S3 resources. While enabled, Block public access (bucket settings) prevents an individual bucket, and its contained objects, from becoming publicly accessible. Similarly, Block public access (account settings) prevents all buckets, and contained objects, from becoming publicly accessible across the entire account.

requirements.name: 1.21 Ensure that IAM Access analyzer is enabled

requirements.name: 1.8 Ensure IAM password policy requires minimum length of 14 or greater

requirements.name: 1.9 Ensure IAM password policy prevents password reuse
requirements.description: IAM password policies can prevent the reuse of a given password by the same user. It is recommended that the password policy prevent the reuse of passwords.

requirements.name: 1.10 Ensure multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for all IAM users that have a console password
requirements.description: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an extra layer of authentication assurance beyond traditional credentials. requirements.name: 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled
requirements.description: AWS IAM users can access AWS resources using different types of credentials, such as passwords or access keys. It is recommended that all credentials that have been unused in 45 or greater days be deactivated or removed.

requirements.name: 1.13 Ensure there is only one active access key available for any single IAM user
requirements.description: Access keys are long-term credentials for an IAM user or the AWS account root user. You can use access keys to sign programmatic requests to the AWS CLI or AWS API (directly or using the AWS SDK).

requirements.name: 1.14 Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less
requirements.description: Access keys consist of an access key ID and secret access key, which are used to sign programmatic requests that you make to AWS. requirements.name: 1.15 Ensure IAM Users Receive Permissions Only Through Groups
requirements.description: IAM users are granted access to services, functions, and data through IAM policies. requirements.name: 1.16 Ensure IAM policies that allow full "*:*" administrative privileges are not attached
requirements.description: IAM policies are the means by which privileges are granted to users, groups, or roles. requirements.name: 1.17 Ensure a support role has been created to manage incidents with AWS Support
requirements.description: AWS provides a support center that can be used for incident notification and response, as well as technical support and customer services. Create an IAM Role to allow authorized users to manage incidents with AWS Support.

requirements.name: 1.18 Ensure IAM instance roles are used for AWS resource access from instances
requirements.description: AWS access from within AWS instances can be done by either encoding AWS keys into AWS API calls or by assigning the instance to a role which has an appropriate permissions policy for the required access. requirements.name: 1.19 Ensure that all the expired SSL/TLS certificates stored in AWS IAM are removed

requirements.description: Enable IAM Access analyzer for IAM policies about all resources in each region. IAM Access Analyzer is a technology introduced at AWS reinvent 2019. Scans show resources that other accounts and federated users can access, such as KMS keys and IAM roles. requirements.name: 1.21 Ensure IAM users are managed centrally via identity federation or AWS Organizations for multi-account environments

requirements.description: Amazon S3 provides a variety of no, or low, cost encryption options to protect data at rest.

requirements.name: 2.1.2 Ensure S3 Bucket Policy is set to deny HTTP requests

requirements.name: 2.1.3 Ensure MFA Delete is enabled on S3 buckets
requirements.description: Once MFA Delete is enabled on your sensitive and classified S3 bucket it requires the user to have two forms of authentication.

requirements.name: 2.1.4 Ensure all data in Amazon S3 has been discovered, classified and secured when required
requirements.description: Amazon S3 buckets can contain sensitive data, that for security purposes should be discovered, monitored, classified and protected. Macie along with other 3rd party tools can automatically provide an inventory of Amazon S3 buckets.

requirements.name: 2.1.5 Ensure that S3 Buckets are configured with 'Block public access (bucket settings)'
requirements.description: Amazon S3 provides Block public access (bucket settings) and Block public access (account settings) to help you manage public access to Amazon S3 resources. By default, S3 buckets and objects are created with public access disabled. However, an IAM principle with sufficient S3 permissions can enable public access at the bucket and/or object level. While enabled, Block public access (bucket settings) prevents an individual bucket, and its contained objects, from becoming publicly accessible. Similarly, Block public access (account settings) prevents all buckets, and contained objects, from becoming publicly accessible across the entire account.

requirements.name: 2.2.1 Ensure EBS volume encryption is enabled
requirements.description: Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) supports encryption at rest when using the Elastic Block Store (EBS) service. While disabled by default, forcing encryption at EBS volume creation is supported.

requirements.name: 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption is enabled for RDS Instances
requirements.description: Amazon RDS encrypted DB instances use the industry standard AES-256 encryption algorithm to encrypt your data on the server that hosts your Amazon RDS DB instances. After your data is encrypted, Amazon RDS handles authentication of access and decryption of your data transparently with a minimal impact on performance.

requirements.name: 3.1 Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for your account and delivers log files to you. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service. CloudTrail provides a history of AWS API calls for an account, including API calls made via the Management Console, SDKs, command line tools, and higher-level AWS services (such as CloudFormation).

requirements.name: 3.2 Ensure CloudTrail log file validation is enabled
requirements.description: CloudTrail log file validation creates a digitally signed digest file containing a hash of each log that CloudTrail writes to S3. These digest files can be used to determine whether a log file was changed, deleted, or unchanged after CloudTrail delivered the log. It is recommended that file validation be enabled on all CloudTrails.

requirements.name: 3.3 Ensure the S3 bucket used to store CloudTrail logs is not publicly accessible
requirements.description: CloudTrail logs a record of every API call made in your AWS account. These logs file are stored in an S3 bucket. It is recommended that the bucket policy or access control list (ACL) applied to the S3 bucket that CloudTrail logs to prevent public access to the CloudTrail logs.

requirements.name: 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls made in a given AWS account. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service. CloudTrail uses Amazon S3 for log file storage and delivery, so log files are stored durably. In addition to capturing CloudTrail logs within a specified S3 bucket for long term analysis, realtime analysis can be performed by configuring CloudTrail to send logs to CloudWatch Logs. For a trail that is enabled in all regions in an account, CloudTrail sends log files from all those regions to a CloudWatch Logs log group. It is recommended that CloudTrail logs be sent to CloudWatch Logs.

requirements.name: 3.5 Ensure AWS Config is enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS Config is a web service that performs configuration management of supported AWS resources within your account and delivers log files to you. The recorded information includes the configuration item (AWS resource), relationships between configuration items (AWS resources), any configuration changes between resources. It is recommended AWS Config be enabled in all regions.

requirements.name: 3.6 Ensure S3 bucket access logging is enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket
requirements.description: S3 Bucket Access Logging generates a log that contains access records for each request made to your S3 bucket. An access log record contains details about the request, such as the request type, the resources specified in the request worked, and the time and date the request was processed. It is recommended that bucket access logging be enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket.

requirements.name: 3.7 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for an account and makes those logs available to users and resources in accordance with IAM policies. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) is a managed service that helps create and control the encryption keys used to encrypt account data, and uses Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) to protect the security of encryption keys. CloudTrail logs can be configured to leverage server side encryption (SSE) and KMS customer created master keys (CMK) to further protect CloudTrail logs. It is recommended that CloudTrail be configured to use SSE-KMS.

requirements.name: 3.8 Ensure rotation for customer created CMKs is enabled
requirements.description: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) allows customers to rotate the backing key which is key material stored within the KMS which is tied to the key ID of the Customer Created customer master key (CMK). It is the backing key that is used to perform cryptographic operations such as encryption and decryption. Automated key rotation currently retains all prior backing keys so that decryption of encrypted data can take place transparently. It is recommended that CMK key rotation be enabled.

requirements.name: 3.9 Ensure VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs
requirements.description: VPC Flow Logs is a feature that enables you to capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC. After you've created a flow log, you can view and retrieve its data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It is recommended that VPC Flow Logs be enabled for packet "Rejects" for VPCs.

requirements.name: 3.10 Ensure that Object-level logging for write events is enabled for S3 bucket
requirements.description: S3 object-level API operations such as GetObject, DeleteObject, and PutObject are called data events. By default, CloudTrail trails don't log data events and so it is recommended to enable Object-level logging for S3 buckets.

requirements.name: 3.11 Ensure that Object-level logging for read events is enabled for S3 bucket
requirements.description: S3 object-level API operations such as GetObject, DeleteObject, and PutObject are called data events. By default, CloudTrail trails don't log data events and so it is recommended to enable Object-level logging for S3 buckets.

requirements.name: 4.1 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for unauthorized API calls
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for unauthorized API calls.

requirements.name: 4.2 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for Management Console sign-in without MFA
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. requirements.name: 4.3 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for usage of 'root' account
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for root login attempts.

requirements.name: 4.4 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for IAM policy changes
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established changes made to Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies.

requirements.name: 4.5 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for CloudTrail configuration changes
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for detecting changes to CloudTrail's configurations.

requirements.name: 4.6 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for AWS Management Console authentication failures
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for failed console authentication attempts.

requirements.name: 4.7 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for disabling or scheduled deletion of customer created CMKs
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for customer created CMKs which have changed state to disabled or scheduled deletion.

requirements.name: 4.8 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for S3 bucket policy changes
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for changes to S3 bucket policies.

requirements.name: 4.9 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for AWS Config configuration changes
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for detecting changes to CloudTrail's configurations.

requirements.name: 4.10 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for security group changes
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security Groups are a stateful packet filter that controls ingress and egress traffic within a VPC. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for detecting changes to Security Groups.

requirements.name: 4.11 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for changes to Network Access Control Lists (NACL)
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. NACLs are used as a stateless packet filter to control ingress and egress traffic for subnets within a VPC. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for changes made to NACLs.

requirements.name: 4.12 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for changes to network gateways
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Network gateways are required to send/receive traffic to a destination outside of a VPC. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for changes to network gateways.

requirements.name: 4.13 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for route table changes
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Routing tables are used to route network traffic between subnets and to network gateways. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for changes to route tables.

requirements.name: 4.14 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for VPC changes
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is possible to have more than 1 VPC within an account, in addition it is also possible to create a peer connection between 2 VPCs enabling network traffic to route between VPCs. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for changes made to VPCs.

requirements.name: 4.15 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exists for AWS Organizations changes
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for AWS Organizations changes made in the master AWS Account.

requirements.name: 5.1 Ensure no Network ACLs allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports
requirements.description: The Network Access Control List (NACL) function provide stateless filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources. requirements.name: 5.2 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports
requirements.description: Security groups provide stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources. It is recommended that no security group allows unrestricted ingress access to remote server administration ports, such as SSH to port 22 and RDP to port 3389.

requirements.name: 5.3 Ensure the default security group of every VPC restricts all traffic
requirements.description: A VPC comes with a default security group whose initial settings deny all inbound traffic, allow all outbound traffic, and allow all traffic between instances assigned to the security group. Security groups provide stateful filtering of ingress/egress network traffic to AWS resources. It is recommended that the default security group restrict all traffic.

requirements.name: 5.4 Ensure routing tables for VPC peering are "least access"
requirements.description: Once a VPC peering connection is established, routing tables must be updated to establish any connections between the peered VPCs. These routes can be as specific as desired - even peering a VPC to only a single host on the other side of the connection.

requirements.name: 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption is enabled for RDS Instances

requirements.name: 2.3.2 Ensure Auto Minor Version Upgrade feature is Enabled for RDS Instances

requirements.name: 2.3.3 Ensure that public access is not given to RDS Instance

requirements.name: 2.4.1 Ensure that encryption is enabled for EFS file systems

requirements.name: 3.1 Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for your account and delivers log files to you. requirements.name: 3.2 Ensure CloudTrail log file validation is enabled
requirements.description: CloudTrail log file validation creates a digitally signed digest file containing a hash of each log that CloudTrail writes to S3. These digest files can be used to determine whether a log file was changed, deleted, or unchanged after CloudTrail delivered the log. It is recommended that file validation be enabled on all CloudTrails.

requirements.name: 3.3 Ensure the S3 bucket used to store CloudTrail logs is not publicly accessible
requirements.description: CloudTrail logs a record of every API call made in your AWS account. These logs file are stored in an S3 bucket. It is recommended that the bucket policy or access control list (ACL) applied to the S3 bucket that CloudTrail logs to prevent public access to the CloudTrail logs.

requirements.name: 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls made in a given AWS account. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service. CloudTrail uses Amazon S3 for log file storage and delivery, so log files are stored durably. It is recommended that CloudTrail logs be sent to CloudWatch Logs.

requirements.name: 3.5 Ensure AWS Config is enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS Config is a web service that performs configuration management of supported AWS resources within your account and delivers log files to you. It is recommended AWS Config be enabled in all regions.

requirements.name: 3.6 Ensure S3 bucket access logging is enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket
requirements.description: S3 Bucket Access Logging generates a log that contains access records for each request made to your S3 bucket. An access log record contains details about the request, such as the request type, the resources specified in the request worked, and the time and date the request was processed. It is recommended that bucket access logging be enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket.

requirements.name: 3.7 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for an account and makes those logs available to users and resources in accordance with IAM policies. requirements.name: 3.8 Ensure rotation for customer created symmetric CMKs is enabled

It is recommended that CMK key rotation be enabled for symmetric keys. Key rotation can not be enabled for any asymmetric CMK.

requirements.name: 3.9 Ensure VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs
requirements.description: VPC Flow Logs is a feature that enables you to capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC. After you've created a flow log, you can view and retrieve its data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It is recommended that VPC Flow Logs be enabled for packet "Rejects" for VPCs.

requirements.name: 3.10 Ensure that Object-level logging for write events is enabled for S3 bucket
requirements.description: S3 object-level API operations such as GetObject, DeleteObject, and PutObject are called data events. By default, CloudTrail trails don't log data events and so it is recommended to enable Object-level logging for S3 buckets.

requirements.name: 3.11 Ensure that Object-level logging for read events is enabled for S3 bucket
requirements.description: S3 object-level API operations such as GetObject, DeleteObject, and PutObject are called data events. By default, CloudTrail trails don't log data events and so it is recommended to enable Object-level logging for S3 buckets.

requirements.name: 4.3 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for usage of 'root' account

requirements.name: 4.6 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for AWS Management Console authentication failures

requirements.name: 4.7 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for disabling or scheduled deletion of customer created CMKs

requirements.name: 4.12 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for changes to network gateways

requirements.name: 4.13 Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for route table changes

requirements.name: 5.3 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from ::/0 to remote server administration ports

requirements.description: Amazon S3 provides Block public access (bucket settings) and Block public access (account settings) to help you manage public access to Amazon S3 resources. By default, S3 buckets and objects are created with public access disabled. However, an IAM principal with sufficient S3 permissions can enable public access at the bucket and/or object level. While enabled, Block public access (bucket settings) prevents an individual bucket and its contained objects from becoming publicly accessible. Similarly, Block public access (account settings) prevents all buckets and their contained objects from becoming publicly accessible across the entire account.

requirements.name: 3.2.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS instances
requirements.description: Amazon RDS encrypted DB instances use the industry-standard AES-256 encryption algorithm to encrypt your data on the server that hosts your Amazon RDS DB instances. After your data is encrypted, Amazon RDS handles the authentication of access and the decryption of your data transparently, with minimal impact on performance.

requirements.name: 3.2.2 Ensure the Auto Minor Version Upgrade feature is enabled for RDS instances
requirements.description: Ensure that RDS database instances have the Auto Minor Version Upgrade flag  enabled to automatically receive minor engine upgrades during the specified maintenance window. This way, RDS instances can obtain new features, bug fixes, and security patches for their database engines.

requirements.name: 3.2.3 Ensure that RDS instances are not publicly accessible
requirements.description: Ensure and verify that the RDS database instances provisioned in your AWS account restrict unauthorized access in order to minimize security risks. To restrict access to any RDS database instance, you must disable the Publicly Accessible flag for the database and update the VPC security group associated with the instance.

requirements.name: 3.2.4 Ensure Multi-AZ deployments are used for enhanced availability in Amazon RDS
requirements.description: Amazon RDS offers Multi-AZ deployments that provide enhanced availability and durability for your databases, using synchronous replication to replicate data to a standby instance in a different Availability Zone (AZ). In the event of an infrastructure failure, Amazon RDS automatically fails over to the standby to minimize downtime and ensure business continuity.

requirements.name: 3.3.1 Ensure that encryption is enabled for EFS file systems
requirements.description: Encryption should be enabled for EFS file systems.

requirements.name: 4.1 Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for your account and delivers log files to you. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service. CloudTrail provides a history of AWS API calls for an account, including API calls made via the Management Console, SDKs, command line tools, and higher-level AWS services (such as CloudFormation).

requirements.name: 4.2 Ensure CloudTrail log file validation is enabled
requirements.description: CloudTrail log file validation creates a digitally signed digest file containing a hash of each log that CloudTrail writes to S3. These digest files can be used to determine whether a log file was changed, deleted, or remained unchanged after CloudTrail delivered the log. It is recommended that file validation be enabled for all CloudTrails.

requirements.name: 4.3 Ensure AWS Config is enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS Config is a web service that performs configuration management of supported AWS resources within your account and delivers log files to you. The recorded information includes the configuration items (AWS resources), relationships between configuration items (AWS resources), and any configuration changes between resources. It is recommended that AWS Config be enabled in all regions.

requirements.name: 4.4 Ensure that server access logging is enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket
requirements.description: Server access logging generates a log that contains access records for each request made to your S3 bucket. An access log record contains details about the request, such as the request type, the resources specified in the request worked, and the time and date the request was processed. It is recommended that server access logging be enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket.

requirements.name: 4.5 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for an account and makes those logs available to users and resources in accordance with IAM policies. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) is a managed service that helps create and control the encryption keys used to encrypt account data, and uses Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) to protect the security of encryption keys. CloudTrail logs can be configured to leverage server side encryption (SSE) and KMS customer-created master keys (CMK) to further protect CloudTrail logs. It is recommended that CloudTrail be configured to use SSE-KMS.

requirements.name: 4.6 Ensure rotation for customer-created symmetric CMKs is enabled
requirements.description: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) allows customers to rotate the backing key, which is key material stored within the KMS that is tied to the key ID of the customercreated customer master key (CMK). The backing key is used to perform cryptographic operations such as encryption and decryption. Automated key rotation currently retains all prior backing keys so that decryption of encrypted data can occur transparently. It is recommended that CMK key rotation be enabled for symmetric keys. Key rotation cannot be enabled for any asymmetric CMK.

requirements.name: 4.7 Ensure VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs
requirements.description: VPC Flow Logs is a feature that enables you to capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC. After you've created a flow log, you can view and retrieve its data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It is recommended that VPC Flow Logs be enabled for packet Rejects for VPCs.

requirements.name: 4.8 Ensure that object-level logging for write events is enabled for S3 buckets
requirements.description: S3 object-level API operations, such as GetObject, DeleteObject, and PutObject, are referred to as data events. By default, CloudTrail trails do not log data events, so it is recommended to enable object-level logging for S3 buckets.

requirements.name: 4.9 Ensure that object-level logging for read events is enabled for S3 buckets

requirements.name: 6.2 Ensure no Network ACLs allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports

If a security group is not specified when an instance is launched, it is automatically assigned to this default security group. Security groups provide stateful filtering of ingress/egress network traffic to AWS resources. It is recommended that the default security group restrict all traffic, both inbound and outbound.

requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: Database logging should be enabled
requirements.description: To help with logging and monitoring within your environment, ensure AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) logging is enabled.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance multiple az should be enabled
requirements.description: Multi-AZ support in AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) provides enhanced availability and durability for database instances.

requirements.name: RDS DB instances should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are not public.

requirements.name: RDS DB snapshots should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: Ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) snapshots.

requirements.name: RDS snapshots should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are not public.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift clusters should have automatic snapshots enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS Redshift clusters have automated snapshots enabled. It also checks whether the snapshot retention period is greater than or equal to seven.

requirements.name: Redshift cluster encryption in transit should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure that your AWS Redshift clusters require TLS/SSL encryption to connect to SQL clients.

requirements.name: Redshift cluster audit logging and encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Redshift clusters. You must also ensure that required configurations are deployed on AWS Redshift clusters. The audit logging should be enabled to provide information about connections and user activities in the database.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift clusters should be encrypted with KMS
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Redshift clusters are using a specified AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for encryption. The rule is compliant if encryption is enabled and the cluster is encrypted with the key provided in the kmsKeyArn parameter. The rule is non-compliant if the cluster is not encrypted or encrypted with another key.

requirements.name: Redshift clusters should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Redshift clusters are not public.

requirements.name: S3 bucket cross-region replication should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) Cross-Region Replication (CRR) supports maintaining adequate capacity and availability.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled with KMS
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should enforce SSL
requirements.description: To help protect data in transit, ensure that your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets require requests to use Secure Socket Layer (SSL).

requirements.name: S3 bucket logging should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) server access logging provides a method to monitor the network for potential cybersecurity events.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should prohibit public read access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by only allowing authorized users, processes, and devices access to AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should prohibit public write access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by only allowing authorized users, processes, and devices access to AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 bucket versioning should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) bucket versioning helps keep multiple variants of an object in the same AWS S3 bucket.

requirements.name: S3 public access should be blocked at account level
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: S3 public access should be blocked at bucket levels
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets are publicly accessible. This rule is non-compliant if an AWS S3 bucket is not listed in the excludedPublicBuckets parameter and bucket level settings are public.

requirements.name: SageMaker endpoint configuration encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) is enabled for your SageMaker endpoint.

requirements.name: SageMaker notebook instances should not have direct internet access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS SageMaker notebooks do not allow direct internet access.

requirements.name: SageMaker notebook instance encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) is enabled for your SageMaker notebook.

requirements.name: Secrets Manager secrets should have automatic rotation enabled
requirements.description: This rule ensures AWS Secrets Manager secrets have rotation enabled. Rotating secrets on a regular schedule can shorten the period a secret is active, and potentially reduce the business impact if the secret is compromised.

requirements.name: Secrets Manager secrets should be rotated within specific number of days
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Secrets Manager secrets have been rotated in the past specified number of days. The rule is non-compliant if a secret has not been rotated for more than 'maxDaysSinceRotation' number of days. The default value is 90 days.

requirements.name: Secrets Manager secrets that have not been used in 90 days should be removed
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Secrets Manager secrets have been accessed within a specified number of days. The rule is non-compliant if a secret has not been accessed in 'unusedForDays' number of days. The default value is 90 days.

requirements.name: AWS Security Hub should be enabled for an AWS Account
requirements.description: AWS Security Hub helps to monitor unauthorized personnel, connections, devices, and software. AWS Security Hub aggregates, organizes, and prioritizes the security alerts, or findings, from multiple AWS services.

requirements.name: SNS topics should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that your AWS Simple Notification Service (AWS SNS) topics require encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

requirements.name: VPC default security group should not allow inbound and outbound traffic
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) security groups can help in the management of network access by providing stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources.

requirements.name: VPC route table should restrict public access to IGW
requirements.description: Ensure that there are public routes in the route table to an Internet Gateway (IGW). The rule is non-compliant if a route to an IGW has a destination CIDR block of '0.0.0.0/0' or '::/0'.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress access on ports 20, 21, 22, 3306, 3389, 4333 from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring common ports are restricted on AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) security groups.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress SSH access from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Security Groups can help manage network access by providing stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress TCP and UDP access from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring common ports are restricted on AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Security Groups.

requirements.name: VPC subnet auto assign public IP should be disabled
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC) subnets are assigned a public IP address. The control is compliant if AWS VPC does not have subnets that are assigned a public IP address. The control is non-compliant if AWS VPC has subnets that are assigned a public IP address.

requirements.name: Logging should be enabled on AWS WAFv2 regional and global web access control list (ACLs)
requirements.description: To help with logging and monitoring within your environment, enable AWS WAF (V2) logging on regional and global web ACLs.

requirements.name: VPC flow logs should be enabled
requirements.description: The VPC flow logs provide detailed records for information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC.

requirements.name: ACM certificates should not expire within 30 days
requirements.description: Ensure network integrity is protected by ensuring X509 certificates are issued by AWS ACM.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trails should be integrated with CloudWatch logs
requirements.description: Use AWS CloudWatch to centrally collect and manage log event activity. Inclusion of AWS CloudTrail data provides details of API call activity within your AWS account.

requirements.name: Backup plan min frequency and min retention check
requirements.description: Checks if a backup plan has a backup rule that satisfies the required frequency and retention period(35 Days). The rule is non-compliant if recovery points are not created at least as often as the specified frequency or expire before the specified period.

requirements.name: Backup recovery points should not expire before retention period
requirements.description: Ensure a recovery point expires no earlier than after the specified period. The rule is non-compliant if the recovery point has a retention point less than 35 days.

requirements.name: ElastiCache Redis cluster automatic backup should be enabled with retention period of 15 days or greater
requirements.description: When automatic backups are enabled, AWS ElastiCache creates a backup of the cluster on a daily basis. The backup can be retained for a number of days as specified by your organization. Automatic backups can help guard against data loss.
